scene_note_en: Plays over the loudspeakers in the contestants' dormitory as the wake-up call every morning. It is used from the first wake-up scene in the middle of episode 1.
Plays over the loudspeakers as the contestants walk through the stairwell to the game arena and after the games end. It is also used in the VIP lounge scenes.

part_label_en: Act 2, Rodelinda's aria 'Spietati, io vi giurai'
scene_note_en: Underscores the montage in which Ki-taek gets taken on as Mr. Park's family driver and the family prepares to push out the housekeeper.
At Da-song's birthday party in the garden of Mr. Park's house, an invited singer performs this aria.
Plays as Hae-jun climbs, in person, the rocky mountain that Seo-rae's husband climbed on the day he died, retracing the case.
Underscores the scene in which Oh Dae-su, having found the private prison that held him, tortures Mr. Park and presses him for answers.
Andy locks the warden's office door and plays a record of this duet over the prison loudspeakers. The prisoners stop in their tracks to listen, and Andy is put in solitary confinement.
In the first treatment session, Bertie listens to this piece loudly on headphones while reading Hamlet's soliloquy. Logue records his voice.
Heard as George VI gives his radio address on the declaration of war in 1939. Only Logue stays beside him in the broadcast room to help with the speech.
Heard after the speech, in the final scene where the royal family steps out onto the palace balcony, and in the epilogue captions.
Heard in the opening titles as the Earth and the sun rise behind the moon. It returns in the scene where an ape first uses a bone as a tool.
Heard when the black monolith first appears before the group of apes. It returns when the monolith is found on the moon and again near Jupiter.
Heard as the Pan Am space shuttle docks with the rotating space station. It returns in the moon-landing scene and over the end credits.
Heard as the lunar shuttle carrying Dr. Floyd's party flies over the moon's surface to the excavation site.
Heard in the scene introducing Bowman and Poole aboard Discovery One on its way to Jupiter.
Heard as Bowman enters the Star Gate near Jupiter. Parts of it are also used in the overture before the film begins and in the intermission.
Kaori plays this movement on stage in the violin competition preliminaries. She ignores the score's markings and plays it her own way.
In the second round of the competition, Kaori plays violin with Kousei accompanying on piano. When Kousei stops partway through, Kaori stops too, and then they start again together.
Kousei plays this étude on stage at the piano competition. His playing falters partway through, but he picks it back up and continues to the end.
Kaori does not show up for the gala concert, so Kousei goes on stage alone. He plays this piece, which his mother loved, in the solo piano version.
Kousei plays this ballade in the finals of the piano competition. During the performance, Kaori, violin in hand, appears on stage.
In episode 3, Jun-young plays "Träumerei" when Jeong-gyeong asks him to play any piece at all. The piece is tied to their childhood and returns up to episode 14.
In the graduation recital in episode 16, Jun-young plays Schumann's "Widmung" in Liszt's piano transcription.
In episode 2, Seon-jae and Hye-won sit side by side at one piano and play together for the first time. It is then used as the drama's main theme.

part_label_en: 3rd movement, Allegro ma non troppo – Presto
scene_note_en: In episode 2, Seon-jae plays the finale of the "Appassionata" with great force. The official clip is titled "Seon-jae playing on the bridge."
In episode 2, when Hye-won tests Seon-jae's ability, this is the first of the pieces he plays in succession.
In episode 2, Hye-won listens to Seon-jae play "April." In episode 5, Seon-jae plays this piece again in Hye-won's practice room.
In episode 5, Hye-won and Seon-jae sit at one piano again and play four hands together.
In episode 8, Hye-won and Seon-jae work on it in a lesson as they prepare for a concerto performance. In episode 10, Seon-jae performs it on stage with an orchestra.
On the day of the performance in episode 10, Kang Mae conducts the "Choral" Symphony with the orchestra and chorus in a hall filled with flood victims.
In episode 5, the Seokran City Orchestra plays this as the final piece of its first performance, under Kang Mae's baton.
In 1939 Szpilman plays this piece live at the Warsaw radio station. German bombing hits the station during the performance.
In the hiding apartment, Szpilman, unable to make a sound, only moves his fingers over the keys while imagining this piece. At the end of the film, he plays it on stage with an orchestra.
Szpilman, hiding in the attic of an empty house, hears this piece from the piano downstairs. The player is the German officer Hosenfeld.
In a ruined house, the German officer Hosenfeld has Szpilman play after he says he is a pianist. Szpilman plays this piece on an old grand piano.
Lieutenant Colonel Kilgore's helicopter unit attacks a coastal village while playing this piece through speakers mounted on the helicopters.
Shinji plays the prelude alone on his cello at home. Asuka, who has just come back, hears it and applauds.
The "Hallelujah" chorus plays in the background while Asuka, inside Eva Unit-02, is subjected to an Angel's mental attack.

part_label_en: 4th movement, Presto – Allegro assai (Ode to Joy)
scene_note_en: The fourth-movement chorus plays in the background as Kaworu descends to the lowest level of NERV headquarters. Earlier, by the lakeside, Kaworu hums this melody.
Wednesday plays an arrangement of the first movement of Vivaldi's "Winter" on the cello.
Plays as a drawing of Wednesday playing the cello begins to move by magic.
Wednesday plays this piece alone on the cello in a dark room, with glimpses of other characters cutting in.
Plays as Wednesday hijacks Enid's driving lesson and drives recklessly with the instructor still in the car.
Plays at Camp Jericho when Wednesday summons Eugene's swarm of bees during the Cadets versus Outcasts contest.
Serves as the theme of the admissions coordinator Kim Joo-young and plays in many episodes. In episode 13 there is also a scene of Kim Joo-young listening to it alone.
Background music, in a piano arrangement, that plays under scenes where the characters' emotions come to the surface.

part_label_en: Act 2, aria 'Der Hölle Rache kocht in meinem Herzen' (Queen of the Night's aria)
scene_note_en: Bae Ro-na sings this aria in front of her mother, Oh Yoon-hee, who told her not to sing and tore everything up.
Having left her father at the bottom of the stairs, Cheon Seo-jin plays the piano in her lesson room with bloodied hands.
At Cheon Seo-jin's recital, Oh Yoon-hee, hidden backstage, sings in her place while Cheon Seo-jin only mouths the words.
Used as background music: an arrangement of the Pie Jesu from Fauré's Requiem with vocals added.
Jin-tae sits down at a piano in the middle of a busy street and plays properly in front of people for the first time.
Jin-tae plays the grand piano, its cloth cover removed, at Ga-yul's house. Ga-yul, who gave up the piano after the accident, listens.
Ga-yul carefully presses a key, Jin-tae picks it up, and the two play a four-hand duet at one piano.
Jin-tae, on stage at the gala concert, plays this concerto with an orchestra. It is a performance scene in the latter part of the film.
Plays as Geum-ja, released after 13 years, tells the evangelist who has come to meet her, "Why don't you live right yourself?"
Underscores many scenes, including the one in which Oh Su-hui first enters the prison.
Plays on a sunny afternoon during exercise time in the prison, as inmates talk about how Geum-ja came to be called "the Witch."
Plays as Geum-ja meets the released Oh Su-hui again and they talk about taking revenge on Mr. Baek.
Underscores three scenes, including one explaining the crime committed by the inmate known as "the Witch" in the prison.
Underscores the scene in which Geum-ja, pursued by kidnappers together with her daughter Jenny, fires a gun.
Plays in a piano version as the Count first joins the gathering where Kouzuki has Hideko read erotic books aloud.
Father Sang-hyun himself plays this aria's melody on a recorder. An arrangement of the piece by Jo Yeong-wook also plays at the beginning and end of the film.
Plays over the opening titles as the elderly Salieri, after a suicide attempt, is taken to hospital on a snowy night.
At a concert at the Archbishop's residence, Mozart rushes in and conducts when his piece has already started. Salieri points out the oboe and clarinet passages in a monologue.

part_label_en: Act 2 finale, Commendatore scene 'Don Giovanni, a cenar teco m'invitasti'
scene_note_en: Mozart stages and conducts Don Giovanni in Vienna. From the audience, Salieri watches the scene in which the statue of the Commendatore appears.
Mozart, on his sickbed, sings this section of the Requiem part by part, and Salieri writes it down. As each transcribed part is added, the piece takes shape.
Plays in the scenes of the funeral procession on a rainy day and the burial in the cemetery after Mozart dies.
First heard when the client in black clothes visits Mozart. It returns in the final asylum scene and carries over into the end credits.
In his makeshift cell in Memphis, Lecter plays this aria on a cassette and listens. While the music plays he attacks two guards and escapes.
In a Juilliard conducting class, Lydia plays this prelude on the piano to explain to a student, Max, who says he won't study Bach.
Lydia rehearses this movement with the Berlin orchestra ahead of the live recording. When the strings become too syrupy, she tells them to "forget Visconti."
Lydia chooses this concerto to program alongside Mahler's Fifth, and Olga, the newly joined cellist, plays the solo.
Plays as Chris, withdrawing by helicopter, sees Elias, left behind in the jungle, chased and collapsing. It is also used in the first scene and the burning village scene.
During a performance of Turandot at the Vienna State Opera, Ethan tries from backstage to stop the snipers targeting the Austrian chancellor.
Joe Kraemer's film score borrows the "Nessun dorma" melody and uses it again in later scenes in which Ethan and Ilsa are alone together.
In the scene where Edward takes Vivian to see La traviata at the San Francisco opera house, "Sempre libera" from Act 1 is heard.
In the same opera scene, "Amami, Alfredo" from Act 2 is also heard. Toward the end of the performance, Vivian sheds tears.
Plays as Danny Ocean's crew, job done, watch the Bellagio fountain show together and then go their separate ways one by one.
In the opening scene, where Nina dreams she dances the prologue of Swan Lake, the music plays in an arrangement by Clint Mansell.
The violinist Tim Fain appears on screen as the accompanist and plays live in several of the ballet scenes in which Nina dances.
Plays during the last act of the premiere, as Nina dances the final scene as the Swan Queen.
Heard in a synthesizer arrangement over the opening titles and the first scene showing Alex and his gang at the Korova Milk Bar.
Plays as Alex attacks George and Dim, who have challenged him, on the riverside promenade. It is also used in the gang's other scenes of violence.
Plays in fast motion as Alex spends time in his room with two girls he met at a record shop.
Alex lies on his bed in his room, playing this movement and sinking into violent fantasies.
Heard as the film music of the Nazi newsreel footage that Alex, undergoing the Ludovico technique, is forced to watch with his eyes held open.
The writer Alexander plays this piece loudly downstairs for Alex, whom he has locked in an upstairs room.
The prelude plays under the slow-motion images of the roughly eight-minute prologue before Part 1 begins. It returns several times in the main film.
Heard in the first scene, as the steamship carrying Aschenbach glides through the lagoon at dawn into Venice. It returns several times up to the final beach scene.

part_label_en: 4th movement, Sehr langsam. Misterioso ('O Mensch! Gib Acht!')
scene_note_en: Heard as Aschenbach, seeing Tadzio pass by the beach hut, begins to write music.
Tadzio tries playing this piece on the piano. Aschenbach recalls the prostitute Esmeralda, who played the same piece.
As Aschenbach, having heard that Tadzio's family is leaving, goes out to the beach, a Russian woman sings this song unaccompanied.

At a memorial service for a former village head, the first movement of the "Moonlight" sounds in the community hall, and a wealthy man of the island is found dead. The sonata is heard in each case that follows.
As an assignment from Professor Tanioka, Chiaki and Nodame play this sonata together on two pianos.
In episode 5, Chiaki conducts an S Orchestra rehearsal in Stresemann's place, but the ensemble falls apart. It is performed again at the R☆S concert in episode 23.
The S Orchestra, conducted by Chiaki, plays this symphony on stage at the school's regular concert.

part_label_en: 1st movement, Moderato · part of 3rd movement, Allegro scherzando
scene_note_en: At the school festival in episode 11, Chiaki plays the solo while Stresemann conducts the A Orchestra. In episode 12, he plays it with Nodame on two pianos.
Chiaki conducts this symphony at the first concert of the newly formed R☆S Orchestra.
Pan Wei plays this piece in the first round of the Chopin Competition. Kai, in the audience, hears Pan Wei play for the first time and is stunned.
Shuhei plays this étude, nervously, on stage in the first round of the Chopin Competition.
At last Kai takes the stage in the first round of the Chopin Competition and begins his performance with this étude.
On the first day of the second round of the Chopin Competition, the favorite, Pan Wei, plays this sonata.
In the second round, Kai takes the stage after Lev and plays this sonata.
On the last day of the finals, Kai plays this concerto with an orchestra. Pan Wei and Lev play the same piece in the finals too (season 2, episodes 7–11).
A live-action scene of the Philadelphia Orchestra playing under blue lighting gives way to animation of abstract lines and shapes.
Fairies, mushrooms, fish and flower petals dance to six numbers from the suite as the seasons change from summer to winter.
Mickey Mouse, apprentice to the sorcerer Yen Sid, enchants a broom behind his master's back, and the workshop is flooded.
Shows the formation of the Earth, the appearance of the first living things, and the rise and extinction of the dinosaurs.
Centaurs, cherubs and fauns hold a festival of Bacchus until a storm raised by Zeus hits them.
On Walpurgis Night the demon Chernabog summons the spirits of the graves to Bald Mountain. They retreat at the sound of the dawn bells, and the music leads into "Ave Maria."
Triangular, butterfly-like wings are chased by black bat-shaped figures, then find their light again.
A calf from a family of flying humpback whales gets trapped in an iceberg, escapes with its mother's help, and soars above the pod and the clouds.
In 1930s New York, an unemployed man, a construction worker who dreams of being a drummer, a lonely girl and a rich husband each get the day they wished for.
A one-legged toy soldier falls for a ballerina doll and protects her from a nasty jack-in-the-box.
Donald Duck, Noah's assistant, loads the animals onto the ark, gets separated from Daisy, and then finds her again.
A spring sprite awakened by an elk brings the forest to life, then wakes the Firebird in the volcano, and the forest is engulfed in flames.
Tom, in tails, plays this piece on a concert stage while Jerry, who lives inside the piano, keeps disrupting the performance.
Elmer Fudd, dressed as Siegfried, jabs his spear into Bugs's burrow and sings "Kill the wabbit" to this melody.
Elmer threatens Bugs for the first time by calling down lightning to show off the power of his spear and magic helmet.
Plays in the chase scene in which Elmer pursues the frightened, fleeing Bugs.
Bugs disguised as Brünnhilde and Elmer dressed as Siegfried dance a ballet together.
After the ballet, Bugs and Elmer sing the love duet "Return My Love," set to this melody with new lyrics.
Plays over the first narration of episode 1 and the scene in which the Imperial admirals gather. It is used in the opening narration of many later episodes as well.
In episode 15, the Alliance fleet, pushed back after its supply lines are cut, gathers at the Amlitzer star region for a final battle with the Imperial forces.
In episode 23, Oberstein advises against stopping the nuclear attack on Westerland, leading into the scene of the burning planet.
At the victory ceremony in episode 26, Reinhard watches the end of Kircheis, who took the blow of Ansbach's attack in his place.
In episode 51, the battle in the Vermilion star region begins between the Imperial forces and Yang Wen-li's fleet, which has driven deep into enemy territory to go after Reinhard.
In episode 82, plays as Yang Wen-li, on his way to a conference, is attacked by assassins aboard a cruiser and falls.

part_label_en: Act 3, the Duke of Mantua's canzone 'La donna è mobile'
scene_note_en: At the start of the film, Jang-ho and Sang-jin are each driving along in their own cars, and this aria plays on a car radio.

part_label_en: Act 3, Cavaradossi's aria 'E lucevan le stelle'
scene_note_en: Jang-ho sings this aria to Sang-jin's piano accompaniment, revealing his talent for singing. The singing was recorded by the tenor Kang Yo-seph.
In the latter part of the film, Jang-ho takes the stage and sings this aria. The singing was re-recorded by the tenor Kang Yo-seph to match Lee Je-hoon's acting.
Plays when Gwang-ho, the owner of a pizza shop, first sees Ji-su playing the piano.
On the night Ji-su returns from meeting successful former classmates, she plays this piece at home all night.
Ji-su plays this piece on the piano to comfort a downcast Gyeong-min. It returns near the end of the film.
Gyeong-min plays this piece in front of an audience at a house concert and is recognized for his skill.
The grown-up Gyeong-min plays this concerto with an orchestra on a concert stage. The adult Gyeong-min is played by the pianist Kim Jeong-won, who also performed the piece.
The Harmony choir from a women's prison sings this song in chorus on a big concert hall stage as the climax of the performance.
Kang Bi-o's signature piece. Kang Bi-o plays it on stage at the first competition in episode 1 and in the face-off in episode 5.
The piece through which Choi Jeong-yo and Kang Bi-o grow close when they first play four hands together. It returns in several later episodes.

part_label_en: No. 10, chorale 'Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring'
scene_note_en: Kang Bi-o and Choi Jeong-yo sit side by side at a single piano and play four hands together.

part_label_en: 1st movement, Grave – Allegro di molto e con brio
scene_note_en: In the final scene of episode 4, Choi Jeong-yo plays this piece while Kang Bi-o watches from a distance.
A piece that Kang Bi-o and Choi Jeong-yo play four hands. In the final episode, the two play it together again.
After her mother dies, the conductor Cha Se-eum plays this movement on the violin at the funeral.
In the final episode's performance, Cha Se-eum plays with the concertmaster Lee Ru-na on two violins with the orchestra.
The opening of the first movement plays under the opening title cards at the start of the film. The pianist is Eileen Joyce.
Laura listens to this concerto on the radio in her living room and recalls what happened with Alec, while her husband does the crossword beside her.
Repeated as background music throughout the story of Elvira and Sixten's flight and life together on the run. The recording used is by Géza Anda.
Plays over the opening titles as Jake LaMotta warms up alone in an empty ring. It returns at the end of the film.
Plays in the color home-movie scenes of everyday life of the LaMottas and their family.
